**Your Role:**  
The **Lead Manufacturing Associate, Upstream** provides hands-on technical and frontline leadership for cGMP cell-culture manufacturing in a multi-product facility. The role supports supervisors by coordinating daily execution, communicating priorities, leading critical upstream activities, and helping resolve equipment and process issues. The Lead Manufacturing Associate serves as a liaison between management and manufacturing associates, promotes clear communication and readiness, and supports the timely production and release of high-quality biopharmaceutical products. This position also leads improvement activities, supports training and development, and helps maintain inspection-ready operations and documentation.

* Lead critical upstream manufacturing activities, including cell-bank thaw, cell-culture expansion and maintenance, bioreactor setup, media and feed additions, inoculation, harvest, and associated cGMP documentation.

* Operate and support Wave and 100L–2000L single-use bioreactors using applicable Cytiva, DeltaV, and MFCS systems.

**About Quilter**
=================

At Quilter, we are helping electrical engineers save time and accomplish more by automating the tedious and time-consuming task of designing printed circuit boards (PCBs). Our small team is composed of experts in electrical engineering, electromagnetic simulation, ML/AI, and high-performance computing (HPC). We are inventing and leveraging novel techniques to solve the decades-old problem of automating circuit board design where today hundreds of billions of dollars are spent. We have raised $25 million in Series B funding from some of the very best and are charging full-speed toward our goal.

No matter where we come from, we're united by a common vision for the future and a core set of values we think will get us there:

* Curiosity

* Conviction

* Rigor

We’re looking for a Senior Software Engineer to work directly with our go-to-market team and customers to turn integration blockers into production fixes and features. Our File I/O team connects Quilter with tools including Altium, KiCad, Cadence Allegro, and Siemens Xpedition, preserving design intent as files move into Quilter and results return to the customer’s CAD workflow.

You’ll work primarily in Python on parsers, exporters, design models, diagnostics, and workflow automation. This role suits someone who enjoys jumping into ambiguous technical problems, collaborating directly with customers, and seeing their engineering work make an immediate difference. You’ll contribute to broader improvements in CAD coverage and fidelity as well as resolving urgent blockers.

You’ll also help build workflows using LLMs and agents to investigate failures, find recurring patterns, and automate repetitive integration work, with reliable checks on the results.

**Location:** This is a hybrid role based out of our Long Beach, CA office, with regular in-person collaboration alongside our go-to-market team.

**What You’ll Do**
------------------

* **Investigate and resolve customer blockers.** Work with customers and GTM to reproduce failures, inspect design data and logs, and identify the cause. Fix File I/O issues and coordinate with partner teams when a problem crosses system boundaries.
* **Ship integration features and fixes.** Own Python changes from design through rollout, including parsers, exporters, and shared representations of boards, schematics, and constraints. Make sound implementation tradeoffs and contribute through code reviews.
* **Verify the complete design workflow.** Turn representative customer cases into acceptance checks and regression tests. Validate that design information survives import and that exported results remain usable in the customer’s native CAD tool.
* **Turn recurring problems into better tooling.** Improve diagnostics and error messages, automate reproductions, and build agentic investigation workflows. Use evaluations and feedback loops to make troubleshooting faster and more reliable.
* **Connect customers’ existing workflows to Quilter.** Build reusable scripts and integrations for design-data preparation and handoffs. Use repeated customer needs to identify capabilities worth supporting in the shared product.
* **Work closely with GTM and engineering.** Help the team prioritize urgent blockers and larger improvements, agree on scope and commitments, and explain findings clearly. Pair with customers, demonstrate fixes, and document workflows they can use independently.

**What We’re Looking For**
--------------------------

* Deep production Python experience, with ownership of maintainable software from design through testing and rollout.
* Experience working directly with customers, partners, or technical users to understand a workflow, diagnose integration problems, and deliver working software.
* Strong debugging skills across unfamiliar code, files, and structured data. You can isolate causes and test hypotheses with incomplete information.
* Clear communication and sound judgment under time pressure. You explain uncertainty, coordinate priorities and dependencies, and follow through on both immediate fixes and lasting improvements.
* Practical experience with LLMs and agentic workflows, including evaluating results and improving the tools and feedback loops around them.

**Nice to Have**
----------------

These are useful backgrounds, not a checklist—we don’t expect any one candidate to bring all of them.

* Hands-on familiarity with PCB design workflows and ECAD tools.
* Experience with parsers, proprietary file formats, vendor APIs, or CAD scripting.
* Experience in customer or integration engineering, including troubleshooting in environments with restricted access to systems or design data.
* Experience building regression corpora, diagnostic tools, or agent harnesses and evals.

**What Success Looks Like**
---------------------------

Customer blockers turn into verified production improvements. More designs move successfully through import, Quilter, and native export; recurring failures decrease, and the tests, diagnostics, and workflow tools you build help the whole team resolve the next issue faster.

**Please note**: We are an equal opportunity employer. At this time, we are focused on hiring primarily within the US, with occasional exception to accommodate exceptional talent.

**What we offer:**
==================

* Interesting and challenging work
* Competitive salary and equity benefits
* Health, dental, and vision insurance
* Regular team events and offsites (~4x / year)
* Unlimited paid time off
* Paid parental leave

Responsibilities:

The Laboratory Assistant will follow the guidelines set by CLIA, and the California Business and Professions Code Sections 1212 and 1269. Unlicensed laboratory personnel (“aides”) are limited to pre-analytical and supportive functions only and may not read, record, result, verify, or interpret any laboratory test. They may not perform any test involving the quantitative measurement of specimens or reagents, conduct mathematical calculations related to test results, perform instrument calibration, or monitor or interpret quality control data used to assess test system performance. Unlicensed personnel shall not participate in any phase of testing that involves result generation, interpretation, verification, or reporting.

All duties must be performed under the direct and constant supervision of a physician and surgeon or a licensed laboratory professional, as defined by California regulations.

Unlicensed laboratory personnel may perform approved activities including specimen collection (patient preparation, labeling, handling, processing, preservation, transportation, and storage), assisting licensed personnel, preparing and storing reagents and culture media, assisting with preventive maintenance and troubleshooting (without calibration or performance verification), and supporting quality control procedures (without interpretation of results). Specimen collection involving venipuncture or skin puncture may only be performed if the individual holds appropriate California phlebotomy certification (e.g., CPT I or CPT II) or other qualifying license, as required by law.

This individual: 1) Performs computer entry, filing, telephone communication, and other clerical duties. 2) Demonstrates professional telephone etiquette and greets patients and visitors courteously. 3) Possesses effective verbal and written communication skills. 4) Demonstrates knowledge of laboratory test terminology. 5) Demonstrates knowledge of phlebotomy practices; performs venipuncture or skin puncture only if appropriately certified per California law. 6) Processes specimens across laboratory departments including pathology, microbiology, immunology, hematology, coagulation, urinalysis, chemistry, and blood bank limited to pre-analytical activities (e.g., specimen handling and centrifugation only in immunohematology). 7) Prepares and processes specimens for reference laboratories. 8) Stocks and orders routine supplies. 9) Maintains cleanliness and organization of storage areas, equipment, centrifuges, and collection sites. 10) Processes and places specimens on laboratory instruments for automated analysis only, without performing test setup, calibration, validation, or result review. 11) With documented training, may assist with preventive maintenance and troubleshooting (excluding calibration and performance verification), assist in quality control procedures (without interpreting results), and perform permitted microbiology support tasks such as primary culture inoculation, slide staining, and subculturing. 12) Performs additional duties assigned by department leadership, including clerical support, communication tasks, specimen transport, and interdepartmental deliveries. 13) Assists Pathology with pre-analytical and clerical tasks only, including specimen receipt, accessioning, labeling, transport, and storage, under direct supervision and within regulatory limitations. 14) Functions as a runner to support laboratory workflow and specimen movement as needed.

Zymo Research is seeking a Bioinformatics Scientist to join the Epigenetics Technology team and lead computational development for epigenomics and molecular assay research. The scientist will curate datasets, discover and evaluate candidate methylation biomarkers, develop statistical models, and build reproducible analysis pipelines in close collaboration with experimental scientists.

This role combines epigenomics, statistical modeling, and software development. The scientist will guide computational strategy, define analytical performance criteria, and support targeted assay development, independent validation, and transfer into scalable research products.

Join us in making a meaningful impact!

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**

  

* Own the computational roadmap for assigned research and assay development projects, defining deliverables, milestones, acceptance criteria, data needs, and technical risks. Coordinate priorities and dependencies with experimental scientists and support bioinformatics teams.
* Curate public and internal epigenomic datasets (methylation, hydroxymethylation). Document sample provenance, quality, relevant metadata, assay platform, genome build, and usage permissions; maintain versioned datasets with clear inclusion and quality criteria.
* Discover and prioritize candidate molecular markers and differentially methylated regions. Evaluate specificity, biological variability, common sequence variants, repetitive regions, assay compatibility, and stability across relevant sample and biological conditions.
* Develop and benchmark statistical models for molecular profiling and epigenetic biomarker analysis. Evaluate feature selection, model assumptions, uncertainty and performance supported by the available data.
* Contribute to other projects requiring relevant scientific and technical expertise.

**Pipeline Development and Validation**

* Build reproducible pipelines for methylation sequencing and relevant reference array datasets, covering quality control, alignment, methylation quantification, filtering, annotation, and reporting. Evaluate conversion efficiency, mapping ambiguity, duplicates, coverage, and batch effects using controls appropriate to each assay.
* Co-design targeted methylation panels with the assay team. Perform in silico assessment of primers, probes, and hybridization capture baits for sequence specificity, common variants, conversion-related sequence changes, and cross-hybridization; use empirical enrichment and coverage data to refine panel design.
* Benchmark analytical methods using reference standards, simulations, and independent sample sets. Separate model development, marker selection, and validation by biological source; assess bias, error, agreement, reproducibility, and robustness.
* Assess robustness to sequencing depth, missing data, DNA input, dataset selection, platform differences, batch effects, and relevant biological variation. Use validated harmonization approaches and prevent information leakage across development and validation datasets.
* Define quantitative reporting metrics, calibration approaches, quality thresholds, and validated reporting ranges. Document uncertainty, investigate unexpected results, and communicate analytical limitations.
* Implement automated quality checks, failure flags, versioned reports, and traceable software releases. * Experience with statistical modeling, biomarker discovery, or closely related quantitative methods, including rigorous study design, feature selection, and independent model validation.

**Required Technical Skills**

* Proficiency in Python and R, Linux or Unix, statistical analysis, and scientific visualization. Experience building maintainable analysis code with version control, automated tests, and documented workflows.
* Experience processing Illumina sequencing data, managing large genomic datasets, and developing scalable workflows using high-performance or cloud computing environments.
* Experience with epigenomic biomarker discovery, dataset curation, method benchmarking, or statistical model optimization.

**Preferred Qualifications**

  

* Experience with targeted methylation sequencing, hybridization capture panel design, multiplex primer or probe design, or analysis of methylation-sensitive qPCR or digital PCR data.
* Experience analyzing DNA variants/SNPs using NGS data and appropriate quality control and validation methods.

Responsibilities:

The Laboratory Assistant will follow the guidelines set by CLIA, and the California Business and Professions Code Sections 1212 and 1269. Unlicensed laboratory personnel (“aides”) are limited to pre-analytical and supportive functions only and may not read, record, result, verify, or interpret any laboratory test. They may not perform any test involving the quantitative measurement of specimens or reagents, conduct mathematical calculations related to test results, perform instrument calibration, or monitor or interpret quality control data used to assess test system performance. Unlicensed personnel shall not participate in any phase of testing that involves result generation, interpretation, verification, or reporting.

All duties must be performed under the direct and constant supervision of a physician and surgeon or a licensed laboratory professional, as defined by California regulations.

Unlicensed laboratory personnel may perform approved activities including specimen collection (patient preparation, labeling, handling, processing, preservation, transportation, and storage), assisting licensed personnel, preparing and storing reagents and culture media, assisting with preventive maintenance and troubleshooting (without calibration or performance verification), and supporting quality control procedures (without interpretation of results). Specimen collection involving venipuncture or skin puncture may only be performed if the individual holds appropriate California phlebotomy certification (e.g., CPT I or CPT II) or other qualifying license, as required by law.

This individual: 1) Performs computer entry, filing, telephone communication, and other clerical duties. 2) Demonstrates professional telephone etiquette and greets patients and visitors courteously. 3) Possesses effective verbal and written communication skills. 4) Demonstrates knowledge of laboratory test terminology. 5) Demonstrates knowledge of phlebotomy practices; performs venipuncture or skin puncture only if appropriately certified per California law. 6) Processes specimens across laboratory departments including pathology, microbiology, immunology, hematology, coagulation, urinalysis, chemistry, and blood bank limited to pre-analytical activities (e.g., specimen handling and centrifugation only in immunohematology). 7) Prepares and processes specimens for reference laboratories. 8) Stocks and orders routine supplies. 9) Maintains cleanliness and organization of storage areas, equipment, centrifuges, and collection sites. 10) Processes and places specimens on laboratory instruments for automated analysis only, without performing test setup, calibration, validation, or result review. 11) With documented training, may assist with preventive maintenance and troubleshooting (excluding calibration and performance verification), assist in quality control procedures (without interpreting results), and perform permitted microbiology support tasks such as primary culture inoculation, slide staining, and subculturing. 12) Performs additional duties assigned by department leadership, including clerical support, communication tasks, specimen transport, and interdepartmental deliveries. 13) Assists Pathology with pre-analytical and clerical tasks only, including specimen receipt, accessioning, labeling, transport, and storage, under direct supervision and within regulatory limitations. 14) Functions as a runner to support laboratory workflow and specimen movement as needed.
